steps.user_message: I need help with my 2023 tax return. I'm head of household in Boston MA. My W-2 from Riverside Hospital shows $91,000. I had $12,500 in 1099 income (IT contracting, 6 clients), $1,560 from Citi savings, and $320 from TD Ameritrade. I have a home office (130 sq ft, exclusive use); rent is $1,720/month for 620 sq ft total. Student loan interest: $3,600 (FedLoan, 2017–2019). I donated $1,350 to St. Mary's Food Bank (have the receipt) have receipt, and had $890 in work expenses. What can I deduct, and should I itemize or take the standard deduction? What forms do I need?
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with tax-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
Thanks — that’s enough to give a clear, practical answer and an estimate. I’ll (1) list what’s deductible, (2) show the key math/estimates, (3) recommend whether to itemize, and (4) list the forms you’ll need and next steps. Quick note: these are estimates/general guidance — for finalized filing or complex state rules, consult a tax preparer.

1) What you can (likely) deduct
- Self-employment (1099) business expenses: ordinary & necessary expenses for your IT contracting (you listed $890). These reduce your Schedule C net profit.
- Home-office deduction: you qualify (exclusive-use, 130 sq ft of a 620 sq ft rental). Using the actual method, your allocable share of rent is deductible on Schedule C as a business expense (approx $4,331/year). You can instead use the simplified method ($5 × 130 = $650) if you prefer; the actual-method number is much larger here.
- Half of your self-employment tax: an “above-the-line” adjustment to income (calculated on Schedule SE).
- Interest/Dividends: interest from Citi savings ($1,560) and TD Ameritrade ($320) is taxable income (reported on Form 1040).
- Charitable gift ($1,350 to St. Mary’s): deductible only if you itemize (Schedule A).
- Student loan interest ($3,600): subject to the student loan interest deduction rules (max $2,500, phases out by MAGI). With your income that deduction will likely be eliminated by the MAGI phase-out (see calculations below).
- Unreimbursed W-2 employee expenses: generally NOT deductible for 2018–2025 (suspended). If the $890 you mentioned is business expenses for your 1099 contracting, they are deductible on Schedule C; if those are unreimbursed W-2 expenses, they are not deductible.

2) Key calculations / estimate (using the actual home-office method)
- W-2 wages: $91,000
- 1099 self-employment gross: $12,500
- Business expenses: $890 (you reported) + home-office share of rent (130/620 × $1,720 × 12 = $4,331) = $5,221
- Net Schedule C profit: 12,500 − 5,221 = $7,279
- Self-employment tax base = $7,279 × 92.35% ≈ $6,722
- Self-employment tax ≈ $6,722 × 15.3% ≈ $1,028
- Deductible half of SE tax (adjustment to income) ≈ $514
- Interest income: $1,560 + $320 = $1,880
- Rough AGI = W-2 + net SE profit + interest − (half SE tax)
  ≈ 91,000 + 7,279 + 1,880 − 514 ≈ $99,645

Implication for the student loan interest deduction:
- For 2023, the student loan interest deduction begins to phase out for single/HOH filers with MAGI ≈ $75k and is fully phased out at ≈ $90k. With the estimated MAGI around $99.6k, you will likely be over the limit and therefore cannot take the student loan interest deduction for federal return.

3) Itemize vs standard deduction
- 2023 standard deduction for Head of Household = $20,800.
- Your reported itemizable amount (charitable giving) = $1,350 (plus any state/local taxes and mortgage interest or large medical expenses you haven’t reported).
- Unless you have additional itemizable items (substantial state income tax withholding or property tax, mortgage interest, large unreimbursed medical expenses above the 7.5% AGI floor, or other deductible items totaling > ~$19,450 more than what you already listed), the standard deduction will be far better.
Recommendation: take the standard deduction for 2023 unless you have significant additional itemizable deductions you haven’t listed.

4) Forms you’ll need (federal)
- Form 1040 (main return)
- Schedule C (Profit or Loss from Business) — report the $12,500 1099 income and business expenses (including the home-office expense if you use the actual method).
- Schedule SE — to compute self-employment tax.
- Form 8829 — Expenses for Business Use of Your Home (if you use the actual-method home-office deduction). If you use the simplified method ($5/sq ft), you do not file Form 8829; instead report the simplified amount on Schedule C.
- Schedule 1 (if applicable) — shows adjustments to income (half of SE tax and other adjustments appear here as part of Form 1040 flow).
- Schedule A — only if you choose to itemize (likely not in your case).
- Keep Forms 1099-NEC (or 1099-MISC), W-2, 1099-INT/1099-DIV, and Form 1098-E (student loan interest statement) for your records.

State (Massachusetts)
- Massachusetts Form 1 (resident return). State rules differ from federal in some respects (student loan interest, deductions, exemptions), so check MA specifics or ask if you want me to look up state rules relevant to your items.

5) Other items to consider
- Estimated tax payments: because you had self-employment income, check whether you made quarterly estimated payments during 2023; if not, you may owe tax/penalties at filing.
- Retirement contributions for self-employed (SEP IRA or solo 401(k)) can be deductible if you made them; deadlines and limits vary — contributions for 2023 may still be possible if you haven’t filed yet (SEP contributions generally can be made up to the business’s tax filing date). Ask if you made any contributions.
- If you prefer fewer forms or want a simpler calculation, you can use the simplified home-office method ($650) — but in your case the actual method yields a much larger deduction.
- Keep receipts and documentation: rent receipts, measurement for home office, charity receipt, 1099s, 1098-E, bank/TD statements.

6) Next steps / clarifying questions
- Is the $890 in “work expenses” for your 1099 contracting work (Schedule C) or are those unreimbursed W-2 expenses? (This matters because unreimbursed W-2 expenses are not deductible.)
- Did you pay any mortgage interest, property taxes, or large state income taxes (or have large MA withholding) in 2023 that would increase itemized deductions?
- Do you want me to: (A) prepare an estimated federal tax calculation/estimate of tax due, (B) draft an email to a CPA with these details, or (C) prepare the list of documents and a step-by-step checklist for filing?

If you confirm whether the $890 is business-related and whether you had significant state/property/mortgage items/withholding, I’ll update the numbers and give a tighter recommendation (and can estimate federal tax owed or prepare a draft return checklist).
